newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UAE group highest bidder for former BCCI unit.
newsitem.headline: UAE group highest bidder for former BCCI unit.

text.p: A consortium led by a United Arab Emirates businessman lodged the highest bid for Pakistan's Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd (HCEBL) on Thursday.

Sheikh Nahayan bin Mubarak Al Nayahan bid 38 rupees per share for the 42 million shares, representing a 70 percent equity stake in HCEBL, which was once part of the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI).
Privatisation Commission chairman Khawaja Asif said after the bidding, shown live on state television, that the commission would tell the UAE group later if its bid had been accepted.
"We have the right to accept or reject this price," he said.

The only other bidder to show up out of nine foreign and local companies that had shown interest in HCEBL was the Fauji Foundation, a private business group run partly as a welfare foundation for retired Pakistani army personnel.
Fauji Foundation's final bid was 37.60 rupees.
The government will retain 20 percent of HCEBL's shares and 10 percent will be offered to its employees.
HCEBL net profit rose five percent in the year ended December 31, over its 1995 profit of 265 million rupees.

HCEBL, a subsidiary of Habib Bank Limited, is the third Pakistani bank to be privatised after Muslim Commercial Bank and Allied Bank Ltd. It was the first time since Pakistan launched its privatisation programme in 1991 that bidding had been shown on live television, in what Asif said was an attempt to demonstrate that the proceedings were transparent and clean.
